design_risks: CM5 has no hardware encoder for either codec ([D-24]/[D-31]), so H.264 and H.265 must both run in software on 4x Cortex-A76. The only community data point (H-20: libx265 vbench Live 10 FPS on Pi 5) and a Raspberry Pi engineer's forum statement (H-19) suggest real-time 1080p60 HEVC is unlikely, and 1080p30 is unproven. Plan for HEVC at reduced resolution or frame rate, or as a non-simultaneous option, until hardware tests prove otherwise.

On CM4, the bcm2835-codec H.264 hardware encoder does not help HEVC. HEVC is pure software on 4x Cortex-A72 with no DotProd (H-05); the 1.8 GHz Pi 400 managed 4.33 FPS in the vbench Live test (H-21), and CM4 has to do the same work. HEVC on CM4 is the highest-risk combination.

tune=zerolatency, which low-latency RTMP/WebRTC needs, forces x265 frame-threads to 1 and disables lookahead and B-frames (H-16). That cuts parallelism and compression efficiency. If tune is not zerolatency, GStreamer 1.26.2 x265enc reports a fixed 5-frame latency regardless of real settings (H-15), which can upset live pipeline latency budgets.

Neither x265enc nor FFmpeg libx265 accepts the TC358743's packed UYVY (H-10, H-13). Every frame needs a software UYVY to I420/Y42B conversion (about 249 MB/s read at 1080p60, H-43), competing with the encoder for CPU and memory bandwidth.

Distro GStreamer 1.26.2 cannot mux HEVC into FLV (H-27; eflvmux only in 1.28, [F-34]). HEVC over RTMP needs FFmpeg 7.1.5 (H-26) or a backported muxer, which risks a split GStreamer/FFmpeg architecture with added IPC and buffer copies.
FFmpeg 7.1.5's FLV muxer has no Opus (H-26), so E-RTMP audio must be AAC or MP3, while WebRTC needs Opus ([F-41]). With HDMI audio required, expect two audio encodes for simultaneous RTMP and WebRTC.

H.265 in WebRTC is not universally playable. Chrome 136+ supports it only with hardware support and no software fallback (H-33); Firefox has no support (H-35); Edge does not enable it by default (H-36). RFC 7742 does not require it (H-32). An H.264 WebRTC track must remain, which on CM5 means potentially two concurrent software video encodes.

trixie's x265 4.1 lacks the 4.2 (+8% vs 4.1) and 4.3 AArch64 optimisations (H-07). Performance measured now may improve only if the product image carries a newer x265, which is a maintenance and security-update burden outside Debian.

Licensing exposure: libx265 is GPLv2+ (or a paid MulticoreWare licence), and neither covers HEVC patents (H-39). HEVC pool royalties are per device: Access Advance quotes $1.111 R1 per >$80 device in-compliance, and VCL Advance (ex-Via LA) charges $0.30 R1 above 100k units (H-40 to H-42). Shipping H.265 encode has a cost and legal-review impact that H.264-only does not.

claims.statement: The DesignWare I2S driver (dwc-i2s.c) reads clock-master vs clock-slave capability from the hardware COMP_PARAM_1 MODE_EN bit. It accepts SND_SOC_DAIFMT_BC_FC (CPU is clock consumer) only if the instance reports slave capability, and always rejects the mixed BC_FP and BP_FC modes. A codec-master link like tc358743-audio therefore needs the RP1 instance labelled i2s_clk_consumer (rp1_i2s1).
claims.evidence: dw_configure_dai(): 'if (COMP1_MODE_EN(comp1)) { ... dev->capability |= DW_I2S_MASTER; } else { ... dev->capability |= DW_I2S_SLAVE; }'. dw_i2s_set_fmt(): 'case SND_SOC_DAIFMT_BC_FC: if (dev->capability & DW_I2S_SLAVE) ret = 0; else ret = -EINVAL; ... case SND_SOC_DAIFMT_BC_FP: case SND_SOC_DAIFMT_BP_FC: ret = -EINVAL;'

verification.final_statement: For DT-probed instances, dwc-i2s.c sets DW_I2S_MASTER or DW_I2S_SLAVE from the hardware COMP_PARAM_1 MODE_EN bit (bit 4). dw_i2s_set_fmt() accepts SND_SOC_DAIFMT_BC_FC only if DW_I2S_SLAVE is set, accepts BP_FP only if DW_I2S_MASTER is set, and always rejects BC_FP and BP_FC with -EINVAL. The RP1 datasheet says I2S0 is a clock producer (master) and I2S1 a clock consumer (slave). A codec-master link such as tc358743-audio therefore has to use rp1_i2s1, which is what the i2s_clk_consumer label points to.
verification.notes: Code checked at dwc-i2s.c lines 495-520 and 747-753. The RP1 Peripherals datasheet section 3.7.1 says 'I2S0 is a clock-producer (master) with up to 4 bidirectional channels; I2S1 is a clock-consumer (slave) with up to 4 bidirectional channels ... the clock direction ... is statically configured.' (https://pip-assets.raspberrypi.com/categories/892-raspberry-pi-5/documents/RP-008370-DS-1-rp1-peripherals.pdf). design_risks: Sample-rate mismatch: the Pi I2S is clock consumer and the dummy spdif-dir codec cannot detect the HDMI rate. If the app opens 48 kHz while the source sends 44.1 kHz, audio runs 8.8 % off with no ALSA error. PACSCORDER must read TC358743_CID_AUDIO_SAMPLING_RATE (0x00981980) or subscribe to V4L2_EVENT_CTRL and reopen ALSA, or force 48 kHz LPCM through the EDID. Detection latency is about 1 s because of polling.

Control location differs by platform: /dev/videoN on CM4 (legacy unicam, media-controller off) versus /dev/v4l-subdevN on CM5 (rp1-cfe). The PCM id string differs too. Use the card id 'tc358743' and discover the V4L2 node through the media graph rather than hard-coding paths.

CM5 support for tc358743-audio is inferred from DT labels (i2s_clk_consumer -> rp1_i2s1, GPIO 18-21) and the overlay-map rule. It is not confirmed by Raspberry Pi docs or tests, and RP1 I2S1 formats and channels are set in hardware. Treat it as a bring-up gate.

Stereo only. The driver fixes 2-ch I2S and bcm2835-i2s caps capture at 2 channels. 8-ch TDM would need driver changes, and on CM4 is impossible with bcm2835-i2s. Compressed or multichannel HDMI audio behaviour is undocumented, so the EDID should advertise 2ch LPCM only.

Enabling the I2S overlay claims GPIO21 as well as 18-20. It conflicts with pwm (default pin 18), gpio-ir (default 18) and audremap pins_18_19. TC358743 VDDIO2 must match the IO board's 1.8 V or 3.3 V GPIO_VREF jumper.

A/V sync clock domains differ. Audio is clocked by the HDMI source (TC358743 audio PLL tracking ACR); V4L2 frames are stamped with CLOCK_MONOTONIC at frame start. In GStreamer, alsasrc becomes the pipeline clock and v4l2src maps frame timestamps through a measured delay. In FFmpeg, -f alsa uses wall-clock and -f v4l2 uses monotonic by default, so add -ts abs/mono2abs or use a single clock domain.

Two audio encoders are needed at once: AAC for legacy RTMP/FLV and MP4 ([F-31]) and Opus for WebRTC ([F-41]). Use FFmpeg 'aac' / avenc_aac or voaacenc, plus libopus / opusenc. opusenc rejects 44.1 kHz, so insert audioresample to 48 kHz, which adds CPU load on CM5 where video encode is already in software ([G-22]).

fdk-aac (better quality, HE-AAC) is non-free, incompatible with the GPL FFmpeg build (x264/x265 linked), and absent from the Pi's FFmpeg and GStreamer packages. Shipping it would make the image's FFmpeg unredistributable. Its licence grants no patent rights, and AAC patent licensing needs legal review whatever encoder is used.
gaps: Compressed HDMI audio (AC-3/E-AC-3/DTS as IEC 61937 bitstream) through TC358743 I2S is undocumented. The public datasheet says nothing on non-LPCM, and the driver sets FS_IMODE MASK_NLPCM_SMODE and AUTO_CMD0/1/2 auto-mute bits whose meaning is in Toshiba's REF_01/REF_02 register reference, which is not public. It may be muted or passed through. DATASHEET REQUIRED (register reference) + HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

Multichannel LPCM (5.1/7.1) sent by an ATEM/camera is not handled. The driver hard-codes CONFCTL AUDCHNUM_2 + I2S, and bcm2835-i2s is 2-channel only. It is unknown what the TC358743 outputs on I2S when the source sends more than 2 channels (first pair, downmix, or mute). The EDID advertised by the driver/userspace also controls what sources send. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED; TDM 8-ch on RP1 I2S1 would need driver and overlay changes (BUILD TEST REQUIRED).

No source shows tc358743-audio actually working on Pi 5/CM5 (RP1 I2S1 in slave mode with 2x32 TDM from TC358743). The labels resolve and a Pi 5 spdif-dir + i2s1 example exists (forum t=391090), but the end-to-end path is unverified. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

TC358743 SDO_MODE1 MASK_SDO_BIT_LENG (0x70) is left at 0 by the driver. The actual valid-bit count and alignment of 24-bit HDMI samples inside 32-bit slots, and so whether S32_LE capture keeps the low bits, is not documented publicly. DATASHEET REQUIRED / HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

The HDMI audio sample rates the TC358743 actually supports are not stated in the public datasheet. The driver FS_SET table spans 22.05-768 kHz, but HDMI 1.4 LPCM is 32-192 kHz. Also unverified: bcm2835-i2s slave capture at 192 kHz (BCK 12.288 MHz) and RP1 I2S1 slave at that rate. DATASHEET REQUIRED + HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

Rate-change handling must be built in userspace: subscribe to V4L2_EVENT_CTRL on TC358743_CID_AUDIO_SAMPLING_RATE (video node on CM4 legacy unicam, v4l-subdev on CM5) and reopen ALSA. Detection latency is up to about 1 s with the default poll. Wiring the TC358743 INT pin to a GPIO with a custom overlay 'interrupts' property is possible but untested. BUILD TEST REQUIRED + HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.

A/V sync across clock domains is unvalidated. The TC358743 audio PLL tracks the HDMI source's N/CTS, video is timestamped with CLOCK_MONOTONIC at frame start, and alsasrc as pipeline clock (GstAudioClock, slave-method skew) does not use driver timestamps. Long-run drift over hours and the right GStreamer clock choice (system clock + driver timestamps vs audio clock) need measurement. HARDWARE TEST REQUIRED.
